en.title: Oasis Directors Reveal Gallagher Brothers' Reunion Was 'Not Much Emotion'
en.summary: The upcoming documentary 'Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger' captures Liam and Noel Gallagher's first meeting in 15 years. Directors Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace share candid details about the brothers' notoriously understated reunion.
en.body:
The wait for **Oasis** fans has been agonizingly long, with the iconic band splitting in 2009 after a famously explosive backstage bust-up. Now, a new documentary, **Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger**, is set to premiere at the Venice Film Festival, offering a first look at the Gallagher brothers, **Liam** and **Noel**, reuniting for the first time in 15 years. Directors **Will Lovelace** and **Dylan Southern** spoke with Variety about capturing this monumental, yet surprisingly subdued, moment.

Filmmakers **Southern** and **Lovelace** aimed for an authentic portrayal, which meant stepping back and letting the cameras roll without interference. In fact, they went as far as to leave the room entirely when **Noel** and **Liam** first met again in a London studio after their prolonged estrangement. This approach allowed for a raw, unscripted encounter, but it also meant the emotional fireworks many might have expected were absent. As **Lovelace** put it, "It’s the Gallaghers, it’s not ‘Dawson’s Creek.’"

## The Unseen Reunion

The documentary promises to go beyond the reunion itself, featuring rehearsal, backstage, and onstage footage alongside the brothers' first joint interview in over a decade. The reunion, which took place for the film's production, highlights the unique and often stoic nature of the **Gallagher** siblings. While fans might have envisioned tears or dramatic pronouncements, the reality was far more characteristic of the brothers' famously blunt personalities. The directors' decision to prioritize an unvarnished look at their interaction, even if it lacked overt sentimentality, is central to the film's narrative.

## What This Means for Fans

For the legions of **Oasis** devotees worldwide, this documentary represents a significant event. The **Gallagher** brothers' relationship has been a central, often tumultuous, part of the band's legend. Seeing them interact, even with a characteristic lack of outward emotion, offers a profound insight into their dynamic and the possibility of future collaborations. The film’s premiere at the Venice Film Festival marks the first major public unveiling of this reunion, igniting anticipation and speculation among the fanbase about what the future might hold for the iconic Manchester band.

## What's Next

**Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger** is slated for a wider release in early 2025. The film's premiere at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival on September 5th sets the stage for its upcoming distribution on Disney+.
